packet.exact_semantic_question: What monitoring frequencies do opaque LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE values (e.g. 05/WK, 01/07, 01/01) establish?
packet.relation_contract: frequency codes must be interpreted for monitoring obligations

candidate_interpretations.statement: Each LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE token has a fixed workspace-defined meaning (e.g., 05/WK = five times per week, 01/07 = once per week) independent of permit narrative.
candidate_interpretations.rationale: No workspace file defines the NN/XX or NN/WK encoding. PASS_TASK.md states that if a definition is not in a workspace file, UNRESOLVED is correct, and that structural CSV correlation is not a code legend.

candidate_interpretations.statement: For calendar-scheduled parameters, each code's frequency is established by joining structured limit rows to the matching permit's Part I MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY column for the same permit number and pollutant.
candidate_interpretations.rationale: Permit tables use human-readable frequencies (Five/Week, 1/Day, 1/Week, 2/month, Once/Quarter, Continuous) that consistently align with structured codes on matched rows, but the workspace never states that the structured token encodes that text. Inference requires a cross-source join not authorized as a code legend.

candidate_interpretations.statement: 09/99 and 99/99 establish ordinary periodic sampling frequencies comparable to 01/07 or 05/WK.
candidate_interpretations.rationale: 99/99 appears only on continuous flow (TM sample type) where permit text says 'Continuous'. 09/99 appears only on WET retest parameters described as '(If required)' additional reporting, not a calendar schedule.

contradictory_evidence.claim: Structured codes are meaningless opaque identifiers.
contradictory_evidence.counterevidence: Consistent one-to-one alignment between each of the eight codes and human-readable MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY text on matched permit+parameter rows across all three facilities (e.g., 05/WK with Five/Week or 5/Week, 01/01 with 1/Day or Daily, 01/07 with 1/Week, 02/07 with 2/Week, 02/30 with 2/month, 01/90 with Once/Quarter or 1/Quarter, 99/99 with Continuous, 09/99 with conditional WET retest rows).
contradictory_evidence.why_not_dispositive: PASS_TASK.md forbids treating structural CSV correlation alone as a code legend; permit text never uses the opaque tokens, so the alignment is inferential.

known_limitations: No workspace file explicitly defines LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE semantics or the NN/XX encoding scheme.
Permit narrative uses notations such as Five/Week, 1/Day, 1/Week, Once/Quarter, and Continuous — never the structured tokens 05/WK, 01/01, 01/07, etc.
Footnotes and conditions (e.g., *1 sampling on five different days; *1 when discharging) modify nominal frequencies but are not encoded in the code field.
09/99 rows are event-triggered WET retests, not periodic calendar schedules.
Codes present in permit text but absent from permit_limits.csv (e.g., Aztec WET Once/Term, GCC WET Once/5 years) cannot be decoded from structured data in this workspace.
DMR_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE sometimes differs from LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE on reported measurements, so DMR-side codes do not provide a standalone legend.

grounding: sources/permit_limits.csv: LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE is populated on 105 limit rows with eight distinct opaque tokens (e.g. 05/WK, 01/07, 01/01, 09/99, 99/99) and no definition column or workspace legend for the field.

judgment.interpretation: Workspace sources do not establish a general decoding of LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE into monitoring frequencies. Permit narrative text supplies human-readable frequencies for matched permit-parameter rows, but no workspace file authorizes those texts as a legend for the opaque tokens. Consistent CSV-to-permit alignment across three facilities is present in the packet but is explicitly non-dispositive. A supported negative finding applies only to 09/99 and 99/99: they do not establish ordinary calendar periodic sampling frequencies comparable to codes such as 01/07 or 05/WK—99/99 appears on continuous-flow parameters and 09/99 on conditional WET retest reporting.
judgment.remaining_uncertainty: Whether each calendar-structured token (05/WK, 01/01, 01/07, 02/07, 02/30, 01/90) encodes the human-readable MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY on its matched permit row; whether a reusable NN/XX or NN/WK encoding scheme exists beyond this workspace; how footnoted conditions (e.g. sampling on five different days, when discharging) modify nominal frequencies relative to the code field; whether DMR_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE could disambiguate any limit-side codes.

proposal.interpretation: No construction change is proposed. A hypothetical permit-crosswalk mapping (joining each limit row's LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE to the matching permit's Part I MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY for the same permit number and pollutant) would assign human-readable frequencies such as Five/Week, 1/Day, and 1/Week to calendar codes, but the frozen packet does not establish that mapping as workspace truth. A standalone codebook mapping (e.g. 05/WK = five times per week) lacks any workspace definition file.
proposal.exact_grounding: Packet contradictory_evidence and known_limitations: permit text never uses opaque tokens; PASS_TASK rules forbid treating structural CSV correlation alone as a code legend; no workspace file defines LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE semantics.
proposal.semantic_delta: Would add interpreted monitoring-frequency semantics to monitoring_requirement_fy2025.limit_freq_of_analysis_code (purpose B require_interpreted monitoring_frequency_code), replacing opaque pass-through with decoded cadence labels or structured period objects. Not proposed because grounding is insufficient.
proposal.remaining_uncertainty: All eight distinct code values would require authoritative legend or an explicitly authorized cross-source join rule; footnote and conditional modifiers are not represented in the code field; codes present in permit text but absent from permit_limits.csv cannot be validated.

children.exact_semantic_question: What calendar-periodic monitoring frequencies do LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE values 01/01, 01/07, 02/07, 02/30, 05/WK, and 01/90 establish when joined to permit Part I tables?
What monitoring obligation does LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE 99/99 establish?
What monitoring or reporting obligation does LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE 09/99 establish for WET retest parameters?

refinement.why_necessary: Retrieved evidence shows materially different obligation types under the same field: most codes align with calendar MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY text in permit tables, 99/99 aligns with continuous flow monitoring only, and 09/99 marks conditional WET retest reporting described as '(If required)' rather than a periodic schedule. A single interpretation rule cannot treat all eight codes uniformly.
